official_excerpts.section: ### How to Set Up a Route
official_excerpts.text: * Select URL **contains** or **is equal to** a particular URL.

official_excerpts.title: Spaces: Distinct Browsing Areas
official_excerpts.section: ### How to Set Up a Route
official_excerpts.text: + **Contains** will route links that contains your text entry, even it's not an exact match. Great options for "*Contains*" are website domains. For example, if you create a Route for URL's that contain "spotify.com", this Spotify link\* will Route automatically to your Music Space. (\*This is a favorite album from our teammate, Brian!)

official_excerpts.title: Spaces: Distinct Browsing Areas
official_excerpts.section: ### How to Set Up a Route
official_excerpts.text: + **Is equal to** will only route links that exactly match your text entry. Make sure to include http://www, if that's how your link loads! This is a great option for very specific URLs. For example, you may use Google Docs across all Spaces, but if should always route to your Work Space, *is equal to* is the right choice.

official_excerpts.title: Spaces: Distinct Browsing Areas
official_excerpts.section: ## Route Sites to Specific Spaces with Air Traffic Control
official_excerpts.text: You can also set up a default Space for links so tabs are automatically opened in the Space of your choice, rather than in Little Arc.

official_excerpts.title: Spaces: Distinct Browsing Areas
official_excerpts.section: ### How to Set Up a Route
official_excerpts.text: If you have a Route set up on a Space that's been deleted, the Route will be deleted as well.

official_excerpts.title: Pinned Tabs: Tabs you want to stick around
official_excerpts.text: * Pinned Tabs are like "Apps" in that they keep you contained within a specific site. If you pin the New York Times, for example, you can navigate anywhere on the New York Times website but clicking a link that would change the tab will open a Peek window, instead of replacing New York Times.
